enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1042 AM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

...New AVIATION...


.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1034 AM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

 - Dry conditions and light winds persist through the work week
   with typical mid-November temperatures. Some patchy fog is
   expected early Tuesday morning.

 - Next potential system arrives late this week which could bring
   more rain chances. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MST Mon Nov 9 2026

Upper low over north-central Texas continues to progress eastward,
leaving New Mexico and west Texas under a very positively-tilted
ridge. Skies have cleared quickly this evening, leaving the region
in a light wind/clear sky weather pattern favorable for patchy
fog. An area of fog/low stratus has already formed over the upper
Mimbres River in Grant County, as well as portions of the Otero
Mesa. Wouldn't be surprised to see this spread in coverage through
the overnight hours into Tuesday morning, affecting much of the
Tularosa Basin, Rio Grande Valley, and Southwest New Mexico
deserts. Will be something to monitor through the night. 

Tuesday looks sunny and mild with very light southwest flow. High
pressure aloft is currently fixed across all of the Southwestern 
U.S, and looks to stay that way through much of the week ahead. 
This will lead to dry weather, mostly light winds, and typical 
mid-November temperatures with lowland highs in the upper 
60s/lower 70s. Not much to talk about weather-wise over the next 
few days.

Upper ridge finally progresses across the Southern Rockies by next
Friday. Both global models depict a fast-moving shortwave swing
across the International Border Friday/Saturday. This would be our
next precipitation chance. Current forecast shows this to be a
chance of rain showers next Saturday, with generally light
amounts. Sunday into early next week looks dry following this 
passage.

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1034 AM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

Mainly VFR with light diurnal winds prevails until a modest
northerly wind shift arrives at the terminals between 06-12Z.
Low-to-moderate confidence in patchy mist developing in southern
Dona Ana County, west of the Franklin/Organ Mountains, after about
08Z, so have mentioned 6SM BR at KLRU. Even lower confidence in
any MVFR visibility at KELP, despite some patchy fog potentially
developing to the north in the Tularosa Basin as well. RAP 
forecast soundings do not show enough surface cooling for mist/fog
at KELP, despite dewpoints hanging in the low-mid 40s F. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 420 AM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

A warming and drying trend continues. Min RH values will vary
considerably with the driest air across the Gila. Winds will be
very light today, and this will limit smoke transport and venting.
Afternoon highs will hold steady for the rest of the week while
min RH values drop. Winds will increase enough to foster gradually 
improving vent categories through the rest of the week. 

&&
